Tarrant County College raised its property tax rate in September, and now it says the drop in property values it reported was off by nearly 36 billion dollars.

Tarrant County College trustees raised the college's tax rate Sept. 10, to 12 cents per $100 of value from 11.228 cents. Budget pressures cited included declining property values.

On Sept. 28, TCC corrected the number: certified net taxable value fell from about $322.9 billion to $319.1 billion, a $3.8 billion drop, not the $39 billion previously reported. The college says it had compared two different measures of value. The rate stays. For a property with the same taxable value both years, it adds $7.72 a year per $100,000.

Trustee Laura Forkner Pritchett, the lone vote against the increase, said a constituent raised concerns about the figures.

Fort Worth's median sale over the last 12 months was $337,000.

Incentives are capped at $6.5 million, including about $3.2 million in waived fees, up to $2.5 million in bridge cost reimbursement and up to $800,000 in impact fee credits. There's a claw-back of about $1 million per anchor tenant that doesn't open within five years.

Grapevine tested more than 9,000 water valves in August, found 32 that don't work, and just hired a crew to fix them.

Grapevine City Council approved a $3.5 million contract with Ruts Construction on Oct. 20 for citywide water and sewer main replacements, valve and manhole replacements and storm drainage work, 95 work items over 12 to 18 months. The first work order is $543,000 for valves.

Testing of more than 9,000 valves in August found 32 that don't work, many on transmission mains. Last winter a 20-inch water main broke at the city's service center, and the emergency repair got costly because a broken valve was stuck open.

A year after DART's Silver Line started running, its bridge over US 75 in Richardson finally lights up at night.

Richardson held a lighting ceremony Oct. 15 for new blue and white accent lighting on the DART Silver Line bridge over US 75, just south of the President George Bush Turnpike. The lights cover the two 400-foot steel arches installed this summer and the bridge's concrete columns.

The city says the lighting improves nighttime visibility and calls the bridge a gateway and visual branding for Richardson, for rail passengers and drivers on US 75. The Silver Line began rail service in October 2025.
